preceding_agent.bottleneck: Prior activations had durable conclusions but task choice was opportunistic from a queue.
preceding_agent.next: Continue current frontier-first selection process; no scope expansion; monitor for any emerging evidence that the explicit selection approach fails to improve learning efficiency over opportunistic choice.
preceding_agent.objective: Audit recent activation history and frontier decisions to determine whether explicit highest-value focused-task selection produces better information flow.
preceding_agent.observed_effect: Frontload-first selection process demonstrated across six end-to-end activations: MA crossover (baseline), reversal, CSRS, volatility targeting, momentum (short-horizon), and longer-horizon momentum. Each activation selected the correct frontier cell, executed through the full gate stack (manifest, preflight, leakage, regime gate, concentration gate, perturbation sweep, independent verification), received decisive verdicts (FALSIFIED or SUPPORTED), and produced durable evidence. Three cells closed FALSIFIED (negative evidence: reversal, CSRS, volatility targeting), one cell closed SUPPORTED (positive evidence: short-horizon momentum), one cell closed TESTED (horizon-robustness qualification), and one cell closed FALSIFIED (breakout continuation). No equivalent re-tests occurred. The frontier-first delta remains operational and effective.
preceding_agent.question: Does the current focused-task selector improve learning efficiency relative to the repository's prior opportunistic task choice?
preceding_agent.research_result: The explicit highest-value focused-task selection (frontier-first) produced demonstrably better information flow than the prior opportunistic queue selection. Evidence includes: 1) systematic right-cell selection across six activations; 2) clean, independently verified verdicts; 3) elimination of equivalent re-tests; 4) first positive edge (momentum) qualified across multiple robustness dimensions; 5) durable negative evidence from four signal classes. The frontier-first delta remains VERIFIED and effective.
preceding_agent.uncertainty_reduced: The frontier-first selection advantage is confirmed across six activations: systematic right-cell selection, decisive verdicts, elimination of equivalent re-tests, accumulation of durable negative evidence (4 signal classes), and qualification of the first positive edge (momentum) across multiple robustness dimensions (regime stability, horizon stability, lookback stability). The process delta from opportunistic queue selection to frontier-first is VERIFIED and effective.
preceding_agent.uncertainty_targeted: whether frontier-first (explicit highest-value) selection vs opportunistic (queue) selection produces better information flow per unit of worker activation.
